overview: The MPS Strategic & Capital Planning Subcommittee oversees the district's long-term facility improvements and multi-year organizational goals. The body manages the prioritization of capital projects, coordinates with state funding programs like the Massachusetts School Building Authority, and addresses operational challenges such as enrollment shifts and space constraints. Since late 2024, the subcommittee has been developing a comprehensive five-year strategic plan informed by community engagement. As of the most recent records, the body is focusing on integrating facility planning with academic grade configurations and finalizing its strategic vision for 2027.

threads.name: Capital Project Prioritization and Budgeting
threads.summary: The subcommittee maintains a multi-year capital plan spreadsheet to track building needs and potential funding sources. Early efforts focused on bundling HVAC and roof repairs at McGlynn and Andrews into city bonding packages to ensure timely construction completion. Kenneth Lord presented a prioritized plan based on facility assessments, which was eventually adapted into a specific format for coordination with city-wide capital planning. The subcommittee regularly votes to recommend updated project priorities to the full School Committee for budget inclusion.

threads.name: MSBA Accelerated Repair Program
threads.summary: The district utilizes the Massachusetts School Building Authority (MSBA) Accelerated Repair Program to address large-scale roof and HVAC needs at aging facilities. Initial planning involved funding mini-assessments for the Brooks, Roberts, and Missituk schools to prepare for the state application window. By late 2025, the MSBA had approved three statements of interest for these projects. The subcommittee continues to monitor the timeline for these improvements alongside other city-led electrification assessments.

threads.name: Elementary Enrollment and Overcrowding
threads.summary: The body addresses acute capacity constraints and enrollment inequities, particularly at the Roberts School. Dr. Suzanne Galusi presented data on rising transportation costs and specialized programming needs that led to the relocation of MEEP preschool classrooms to the Missituk School. A strategic space planning task force was created to manage community engagement regarding space utilization. Recent discussions focus on aligning these facility decisions with a broader middle school grade reconfiguration study.

threads.name: Strategic Planning and Community Engagement
threads.summary: The subcommittee is leading the development of a district-wide strategic plan to establish a five-year mission and vision. The process involves two phases: a community input phase utilizing surveys and focus groups, followed by an administrative action plan. Efforts have been made to reach underrepresented groups and avoid community survey fatigue by coordinating with high school feasibility studies. The body has set a target to finalize the draft plan by February 2027 and is seeking technical consultant assistance to lead the drafting process.

threads.name: Building Security and Systems Maintenance
threads.summary: Immediate facilities work frequently targets security infrastructure and mechanical system failures. The subcommittee recommended a major project for district-wide keyless fobs, electronic door locks, and integrated camera intercoms. Other prioritized maintenance includes freight elevator motor repairs at Medford High School and the installation of network closet mini-splits. While some projects like the security upgrades were slated for completion by early 2026, others have faced challenges regarding funding allocation and coordination.

threads.name: Playground Feasibility and Development
threads.summary: Playground renovations are a recurring priority due to site limitations and aging equipment at elementary schools. The subcommittee identified the Roberts playground as a top priority but noted significant space and parking constraints that require further exploration. The body has explored using Community Preservation Act funds for design and feasibility studies at multiple school sites. Recent updates include a proposed design study for three remaining school playgrounds to determine future renovation costs.
